Okay so um, I was at the airport yesterday and I'm in the security line, right, and the guy goes sir, did you pack your own bag. And I'm like, who else is packing my bag? My mother? She's been dead since two thousand nine but sure, she did it, she came down for the weekend. And you know the whole thing is, airports treat adults like toddlers with luggage. Take your shoes off. And then I get to the gate and I buy a pretzel, a soft pretzel, and it's eleven dollars. Eleven dollars! It's flour and regret. It's a bread shape that says I give up. And I paid it, because I'm a coward at the airport, you know, I'm not gonna argue about a pretzel with a guy who has a radio.

My mother, God rest her, hated flying. She'd say if God wanted us to fly he would have given us better snacks at the gate. And honestly, turns out she was right about the pretzels. She was right about a lot of things, which is the annoying part about dead people, they don't have to deal with the consequences of being right.
